page: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. It features 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a balanced performance profile for standard workloads. The instance achieves average (middle 50%) scores in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. However, raw compute stress tests show some limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance landing in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks is also on the weaker side (bottom 25%), though cached small-block reads perform at an average level.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5a.2xlarge offers a dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile that balances compute resources without the premium of local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, Redis key-value operations, and basic text or image processing, where it demonstrates average throughput. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded decompression tasks due to its memory bandwidth and multi-core constraints.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation at 3.3 GHz but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average capabilities across standard tasks, including Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. However, it exhibits weaker performance in heavy multi-core stress tests and large-block memory bandwidth. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, the c5a.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-effective for moderate compute workloads, such as web serving, Redis database operations, and light image processing, while remaining constrained for memory-heavy or large-scale machine learning tasks.
